answer: A sybil farm can copy keys instantly, but it cannot copy elapsed time. Make each identity anchor its standing to an unbroken verifiable-delay chain: a sequential pulse of hashes that must be computed one step at a time, with periodic checkpoints signed in. Splitting one machine across a hundred names slows every chain to a crawl, so only identities with dedicated, continuous time advance at full rate. Like saffron, value comes from slow accumulation that cannot be rushed; a newcomer swarm arrives with no history and earns trust only as fast as real time passes.
